text:
rachel: quick sync on derived-token TTLs when a service proxies a request and we mint a child token. we need a clear semantics doc so clients & auditors aren't surprised.

dev: short version: three modes we debated: inherit-truncate (child TTL = min(parent_ttl, route_max)), fresh-fixed (issuer picks fresh ttl), and explicit-approve (route opt-in).

omar: i slightly prefer inherit-truncate as the safe default for least surprise, but with two caveats: 1) explicit rejection on role-expansion, 2) org_max cap (e.g. 24h) regardless of parent.

tricia: role-expansion detection is critical. implement check: projected_roles \u2216 parent_roles -> fail unless route_override=true. we'll need a small library function to compare role sets and surface the differences in logs.

rachel: agree. also decide failure-mode: do we reject issuance or auto-truncate? my preference: rollout with reject first (safer), then switch to auto-truncate later behind telemetry.

dev: rollout plan makes sense. if we reject, clients will break loudly and fix. but for user-facing background jobs that rely on silent truncation we must offer an admin-approved extension flow.

omar: extension flow idea: route requests extension with signed admin ticket. issuance records extension_id in audit. sample api: POST /mint?route=foo&extend=true body: { admin_ticket: "TKT-123" }

infra-bot: deployment note: token cache keys must include (parent_id, route_id, ttl_mode, projection_hash). otherwise derived tokens with different policies collide.

tricia: telemetry we should emit: derived_issue.total, derived_issue.rejected.role_expansion, derived_issue.truncated.count, avg_derived_ttl.ms, lineage.max_depth. slice these by route & org.

rachel: security: operator/platform tokens should not be allowed to be proxied by default. add allowlist: proxy_allowed: [service-a, service-b]. document strong warning in console.

dev: verifier change: TTL enforcement needs to be baked into the verifier as well as issuer. if someone forges a child token with longer TTL it should be rejected by verifier if it exceeds parent or org caps. that means tokens carry parent_id and issued_expiry and we check chain on verify.

omar: that implies we keep parent metadata available to verifier. either include parent_expiry in token claims (signed) or verifier must fetch parent metadata from store. prefer claims to avoid synchronous lookups, but watch token size.

tricia: KMS consideration: derived tokens should be signed with a derived key context or a key_version that records "derived_from: <parent_kid>" to make key provenance auditable. audit-bot: opened ticket SEC-724 for KMS policy review.

rachel: sample route config (yaml):

  auth:
    mode: inherit-truncate   # enum: inherit-truncate | fresh-fixed | explicit-approve
    max_ttl: 3600           # seconds
    allow_role_expansion: false
    proxy_allowed: false

dev: we should include ttl_truncate_behavior enum: reject | truncate | warn. default during rollout = reject. after 2w switch to truncate with warnings.

tricia: add a lint check in CI that flags routes with allow_role_expansion: true so reviewers see potential security widening.

rachel: migration phasing proposal:
- phase 0: implement checks + auditor logs but keep no change to default behavior
- phase 1 (opt-in): new enum present, default still legacy, routes can opt-in to inherit-truncate with reject on expand
- phase 2 (enforce): after 10 days low rejections, flip default to inherit-truncate + truncate_behavior=truncate (with warnings)
- phase 3 (strict): add org_max cap enforcement and block operator tokens from proxying by default

dev: metrics guardrails: stop the flip if derived_issue.rejected.role_expansion > 0.5% for any critical route. we should include a kill-switch flag.

omar: also handle long-lived parent tokens: if parent_ttl > org_max then treat as parent_ttl = org_max for derived calculation and emit a warning.

audit-bot: recommendation: emit a structured audit event on issuance: {event: "derived_issue", parent_id, child_id, issued_ttl, route, actor, role_delta}. keep payload under 4KB.

tricia: UX: console should show "token lineage" view (parent -> children) with quick toggle to show only long-lived descendants. helps SREs investigate leaks.

rachel: ACTIONS:
- dev: draft short RFC with enums, verifier checks, KMS implications, and migration plan (due Thu)
- omar + tricia: run route-audit to tag routes that expand roles or require long-lived derivations (due Tue)
- infra: implement cache-key and telemetry fields (create ticket)
- audit-bot: add audit event schema to SEC-724 and wire to logging pipeline

dev: will include example curl flows and error codes (HTTP 422 for role expansion reject).

omar: i'll prototype role-diff util and put it in authn-lib. open PR next week.

tricia: minor note: make sure SAM/STS style short-lived tokens aren't treated as parentless; we should accept upstream STS tokens but enforce provenance claim.

rachel: thanks all. i'll put RFC draft in #rfc when ready and tag reviewers. :rocket:
